questions.stem: How does a non-competitive inhibitor reduce enzyme activity?

options.text: It competes with the substrate for the active site
It binds to a site other than the active site, changing the shape of the active site
It breaks down the enzyme permanently
It removes the substrate from the solution

questions.explanation: A non-competitive inhibitor binds to an allosteric site (not the active site), which causes a conformational change in the enzyme that alters the shape of the active site, preventing substrate binding.
